findings.heading: Constructing the plot / Construindo o gráfico
findings.proposition: English tells the reader to PREVENT bars from disappearing BY MAKING the count-axis limits auto-adjust to the data ('Prevent it by having your count-axis limits auto-adjust to your data'); the Portuguese says the opposite, 'Evite que os limites do eixo de contagem se ajustem automaticamente aos seus dados' = prevent the count-axis limits FROM auto-adjusting to your data.
findings.reader_consequence: The Portuguese reader is told to avoid the exact remedy the English recommends, so they keep hard-coded axis limits. On routinely updated data a bar that exceeds the fixed limit then vanishes or is silently truncated, which is the failure the DANGER box exists to prevent.

findings.heading: Likert scale / Escala de Likert
findings.proposition: The prose states the table below shows the Likert survey data, with a `status` column and 8 questions on a 4-point scale; in English the chunk beside it renders `DT::datatable(likert_data, ...)`, but in Portuguese the chunk renders `DT::datatable(head(linelist, 10), ...)`, i.e. the Ebola case linelist.
findings.reader_consequence: The Portuguese reader sees the Ebola linelist (case_id, dates, age, gender) where the text promises respondent status and Q1-Q8 Likert responses. They cannot check the input shape for the whole Likert section and may conclude they imported the wrong dataset or that `likert_data` has linelist columns.

findings.heading: apyramid package / Pacote apyramid - Linelist data
findings.proposition: The prose names the argument to add as `proporcional = VERDADEIRO`; the code chunk immediately beside it (and the apyramid API) uses `proportional = TRUE`.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader who copies the argument from the sentence writes `proporcional = VERDADEIRO` and gets an R error (unused argument / object 'VERDADEIRO' not found), because neither the argument name nor the logical literal is translatable in R.

findings.heading: apyramid package / Pacote apyramid
findings.proposition: English says the package help page is opened by entering `?age_pyramid`; Portuguese says to enter `?Age_pyramid` with a capital A, which is not the name of the function or of any help topic.
findings.reader_consequence: The Portuguese reader types `?Age_pyramid` and R answers 'No documentation for Age_pyramid', so they do not reach the help page the sentence points them to.

findings.heading: Aggregated data / Dados agregados
findings.proposition: The display chunk that follows the `pivot_longer()` step is labelled as showing the aggregated data ('Visualize os dados agregados'); in English it renders `DT::datatable(demo_agg_long, ...)`, but in Portuguese it renders `DT::datatable(head(linelist, 5), ...)`.
findings.reader_consequence: The Portuguese reader never sees the long-format table (age_cat5, gender, counts) that the next `age_pyramid(count = "counts")` call depends on, and instead sees the raw linelist, so they cannot verify what `pivot_longer()` produced or why `count = "counts"` is the right argument.
